content.user_title: Configure Neon and Drizzle Database Workflows
content.value_statement: Database setup can become inconsistent when connection code, schemas, and migrations are undocumented. This skill provides a focused Neon and Drizzle workflow for TypeScript projects.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to initialize a Neon serverless Postgres connection with Drizzle ORM.
Identifies the documented locations for database connection and schema definitions.
Shows basic Drizzle select and insert query patterns.
Lists the documented authentication and application database tables.
Describes Drizzle migration generation and schema push commands.
limitations: It does not create or modify database files by itself.
It does not validate database credentials or network connectivity.
It does not provide rollback, backup, or production deployment procedures.
It only documents Neon Postgres and Drizzle ORM patterns.

use_cases.title: Start a Neon connection
use_cases.description: Set up the documented Neon and Drizzle connection pattern for a TypeScript application.

use_cases.title: Review database structure
use_cases.description: Locate the documented schema file and understand the listed authentication and application tables.

use_cases.title: Plan schema migrations
use_cases.description: Generate and review Drizzle migrations before applying them in a controlled environment.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the database stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the database stack documented by this skill and the role of Neon and Drizzle.

prompt_templates.title: Set up the connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure the documented Neon and Drizzle connection. Explain how to protect DATABASE_URL.

prompt_templates.title: Write a safe query
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a Drizzle query using the documented schema. Explain how to avoid exposing user data.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration checklist for a Drizzle schema change. Include review, backup, staging, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Where is the database connection configured?
output_examples.output: The skill documents the connection in db/index.ts. It uses the Neon serverless driver and Drizzle ORM.

output_examples.input: What tables are listed in the schema?
output: Authentication tables: users, sessions, accounts, and verifications.

output_examples.input: How should I apply a schema change?
output_examples.output: Generate and review the migration first. Test it in staging, create a backup, and confirm the target environment before applying it.

best_practices: Store DATABASE_URL in protected environment configuration and never log it.
Use parameterized Drizzle query builders instead of constructing raw SQL strings.
Review and test migrations in staging before applying them to production.
anti_patterns: Do not commit database URLs or credentials to source control.
Do not run schema push commands against production without backups and review.
Do not use example email values or incomplete inserts as production data logic.

faq.question: What database does this skill document?
faq.answer: It documents Neon, a serverless Postgres service.

faq.question: Which ORM does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Drizzle ORM with the Neon HTTP driver.

faq.question: Where is the connection configured?
faq.answer: The skill identifies db/index.ts as the connection location.

faq.question: Where are schemas defined?
faq.answer: The skill identifies db/schema.ts as the schema location.

faq.question: How should DATABASE_URL be handled?
faq.answer: Treat it as a secret. Store it securely and never commit or log it.

faq.question: Is schema push safe for production?
faq.answer: Not without review, backups, staging validation, and explicit confirmation of the target environment.
